correctness.rationale: For \(0<r<1\), \(H=aP_u-bP_v\) has opposite-sign eigenvalues with gap \(q\); the exact interpolation \(|H|=(a-b)H/q+(2ab(1-r^2)/q)I\) yields \(\det D=k(a+b+q)\) and \(u^*D^\dagger v=\langle u,v\rangle/(a+b+q)\). This proves the stated rank-one operator identity and two-dimensional spectrum; \(r=0,1\) follow by direct formulas. At \(a=b=1\), the substitution \(t=r/(1+\sqrt{1-r^2})\) reduces the negative eigenvalue magnitude to \(t(1-t)^2/[2(1+t^2)]\); its derivative factors through the strictly increasing cubic \(t^3+t^2+3t-1\), giving a unique global maximizer and exact sharp constant. Translation covariance proves the universal if-and-only-if scalar threshold; an exact two-dimensional witness has minimum eigenvalue \(1-3\sqrt2/4\). The embedded standalone code checks exact symbolic identities and 900 random matrix cases, with no inference from finite samples to the universal claim.

value.rationale: The symmetric three-matrix operation is a new structural tool for sharp metric-cotype bounds in trace-class geometry. Determining whether this averaging-like map respects a fundamental order cone is a natural gap not resolved by norm-distance control. The complete rank-one eigenvalue formula detects an intrinsically noncommutative boundary, shows two-dimensional minimality, and gives an exact dimension-independent optimal positive-definite scalar correction for all normalized rank-one projection triples. The cubic sharp threshold is a motivated uniform positivity invariant rather than an arbitrary finite calculation, and distinguishes this map from genuinely positive matrix medians.
